text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The number of drug seizures at Stockholm's Arlanda airport has doubled in the first half of 1997 compared to a year ago. The biggest increase was in cocaine and opium shipments.

- The property market is back on the rise again with more overseas investors interested in the sector. Since autumn last year properties worth at least 11 billion crowns have changed hands. Sector analysts said the property market is in the process of restructuring.
- Swedish householders have started to borrow more money again as the sharemarket rises. Nordbanken analysts said net lending rose significantly in 1996 for the first time in many years.

- A consortium led by a division of international engineer ABB has won a big order in China in the city of Hefei in Anhui province, west of Shanghai. The total order is worth $650 million with ABB's share amounting to around $300 million.
- Investment company Ratos has joined the list of Swedish companies fleeing the main A-list on the Stockholm bourse for the smaller O-list to avoid a new, punitive wealth tax.

- Since it became known that Percy Barnevik would take over as chairman at Investor, the investment arm of the powerful Wallenberg family, the value of the Wallenberg's 10 biggest companies on the Stockholm bourse has risen by 169 billion crowns, or three billion crowns a day. The market is expecting more changes amid rumours that Finnish UPM Kymmene's sale of Nokia shares could lead to some deal for Swedish forestry group Stora.
- Financier Adolf Lundin will list his mining company Tenke Mining Corp on the Stockholm bourse this autumn. A group of Swedish analysts visited the company's land in the Congo last week.

- Negotiations betwen telecoms group Ericsson and computer company Cisco have intensified, according to Cisco's Goran Strandberg. Cisco's ambition is that Ericsson becomes one of its 10 strategic partners.
